View coordinates, elevation, and time zones for 500+ major airports worldwide. ### What is an IATA airport code? An IATA airport code is a three-letter alphanumeric code assigned by the International Air Transport Association (IATA) to identify airports worldwide. Kennedy International Airport in New York, LHR for Heathrow in London, and DXB for Dubai International. These codes are used on boarding passes, baggage tags, airline tickets, and flight booking systems to uniquely identify airports. ### What is the difference between an IATA code and an ICAO code? IATA codes are three-letter identifiers (e.g., LAX) used primarily in commercial aviation — on tickets, flight booking systems, and baggage handling. ICAO codes are four-letter identifiers (e.g., KLAX) assigned by the International Civil Aviation Organization and are used in air traffic control, flight planning, weather reports (METARs), and NOTAMs. Most airports have both; small or military airports may have only an ICAO code. ### How are IATA airport codes assigned? IATA codes are assigned by IATA upon application from the airport operator. The three letters are often derived from the airport or city name (e.g., ORD for O'Hare — originally 'Orchard Field'), but there is no strict rule — they are just unique identifiers within the IATA system. ### How a

Runway width, often referred to as the lateral dimension of a runway, is a foundational parameter in airport planning, engineering, and daily operations. Unlike runway length (which is associated with takeoff and landing performance), runway width ensures lateral safety margins for aircraft ground handling, crosswind operations, and the effective placement of markings and lighting. Correctly designed runway width is essential for safe, efficient, and future-proof airport infrastructure. [...] How is runway width defined in airport design? : Runway width is the straight-line, perpendicular distance between the edges of the prepared, load-bearing surface of a runway. It excludes shoulders, blast pads, and safety areas, focusing solely on the pavement or surface designed for aircraft movement. This dimension is a critical safety and operational parameter, determined by the largest, most demanding aircraft expected to use the runway regularly.
